t.2.3.2: Ah, I am supremely pleased, and my power is beyond compare, since you desire my eldest and beloved son to be established as crown prince.
t.2.3.1: Accepting the lotus-like folded hands that they had raised on every side, the king spoke to them words that were both pleasing and beneficial.
t.2.3.3: Having thus honored those brahmins in return, the king spoke these words to Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva, while the others listened.
t.2.3.4: This is the glorious and auspicious month of Caitra, when the forests are in bloom; let everything be made ready for Rāma's installation as crown prince.
t.2.3.5: Approaching the lord of the world, the two bulls among the twice-born, pleased and filled with joy, said, "It has been done," reporting that all was carried out just as he had commanded.
t.2.3.7: Promising "So be it," Sumantra, at the king's command, brought Rāma, the best of chariot-warriors, there by chariot.
t.2.3.6: Then the radiant king spoke these words to Sumantra: "Let Rāma, the self-disciplined one, be brought here by you quickly."
t.2.3.8: Then the rulers of the earth from the east and the north, from the west and the south, seated there at that time, attended upon King Daśaratha.
t.2.3.10: In their midst, like Vāsava amid the Maruts, that royal sage, standing in his palace, saw his son approaching in a chariot.
t.2.3.9: Mlecchas and Āryas, and others too who dwelt in the forests and on the mountain borders, all waited upon him in homage, as the gods attend upon Vāsava.
t.2.3.11: Him who resembled the king of the Gandharvas, whose manliness was renowned in the world, long-armed, of great strength of spirit, moving with the gait of a rutting elephant.
t.2.3.12: Rāma, whose face was lovely as the moon, exceedingly pleasing to behold, who by his beauty, nobility and virtues captivated the eyes and hearts of men.
t.2.3.14: Having helped Rāghava down from the excellent chariot, Sumantra followed behind him with joined palms as he went toward his father.
t.2.3.13: Gazing at him as he approached, like a rain-cloud bringing relief to creatures scorched by the summer heat, the lord of men could not have his fill of looking.
t.2.3.15: That bull among men, Rāghava, together with the charioteer, ascended that palace resembling a peak of Kailāsa in order to see the king.
t.2.3.16: With joined palms, Rāma approached and, bowing low near his father, announced his own name and paid homage at his father's feet.
t.2.3.17: Seeing him bowing at his side with hands folded in reverence, the king took hold of him by his joined hands, drew him close, and embraced his beloved son.
t.2.3.19: Having attained that excellent seat, Rāghava illumined it, as the spotless sun at its rising illumines Mount Meru with its own radiance.
t.2.3.18: And to him, to Rāma, the glorious king assigned a splendid and excellent seat, made ready and adorned with gems and gold.
t.2.3.20: Illuminated there by him, that assembly shone forth like the autumn sky, its planets and stars unclouded, made radiant by the moon.
t.2.3.22: Addressing his son with a smile, the king, best among those blessed with sons, spoke these words to him, as Kaśyapa spoke to Indra, lord of the gods.
t.2.3.21: Gazing upon him, his beloved son, the king rejoiced, as if he were beholding his own adorned self reflected on the surface of a mirror.
t.2.3.24: Since these subjects have been won over by you through your own virtues, therefore, under the conjunction of the Puṣya star, receive the office of heir apparent.
t.2.3.23: Born of my eldest wife, a worthy queen, you are a son worthy of her. O Rāma, you are my own beloved son, foremost in virtues.
t.2.3.25: Of your own will and by your very nature you are disciplined and virtuous; yet, though you are virtuous, out of affection, my son, I will tell you what is for your good.
t.2.3.26: Adopting still greater discipline, be ever one whose senses are conquered, and you should abandon the vices that arise from desire and anger.
t.2.3.27: Conducting yourself with both indirect and direct modes of conduct, win the affection of all your subjects, beginning with your ministers.
t.2.3.28: He who rules the earth with his subjects contented and devoted to him, his friends rejoice like the immortals on obtaining the nectar of immortality. Therefore, my son, conduct yourself only after first restraining yourself.
t.2.3.29: Hearing that, the friends of Rāma, eager to do what pleased him, hastened and quickly approaching, reported it to Kausalyā.
t.2.3.30: Kausalyā, foremost among women, bestowed gold, cows and jewels of many kinds upon those who brought her the joyful news.
t.2.3.31: Then Rāghava, having saluted the king, mounted his chariot and went to his own splendid dwelling, honored by throngs of people.
t.2.3.32: And those citizens too, having then heard that speech of the king, as though they had gained a cherished prize, took leave of the lord of men, went to their homes, and, exceedingly delighted, worshipped the gods.
